item.title: Parents Have Right To Choose Where To Buy School Uniforms, Ministry Says
item.description: The Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education has reiterated that public schools cannot compel parents to purchase uniforms from the school, as this infringes on their right to choose freely.

item.title: Education ministry seeks control of BEAM to end payment delays
item.description: The Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education says there are proposals to remove the Basic Education Assistance Module (BEAM) from the Ministry of Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare and place it directly under the education ministry to allow faster disbursement of funds to schools.

item.title: Bid launched to extend Zimbabwe president’s term in office
item.description: President Mnangagwa's term in office is due to end in 2028 but a bill could open the way for him to extend that time.

item.title: How Zimbabwe’s proposed constitutional amendments are likely aimed at protecting Tagwirei against Chamisa
item.description: Fear is often the silent architect of the most outrageous political maneuvers.

item.title: Dismantling Nick Mangwana’s deceitful Botswana comparisons in defending Zimbabwe’s constitutional power grab
item.description: It is remarkable the lengths to which a desperate hunger for power can drive people.

item.title: What is damaged in Zimbabwe are the people in power and not the constitution
item.description: It is said that a poor carpenter always blames his tools.

item.title: Zimbabwe’s constitutional crisis exposes the reality of the ‘prisoner of power’
item.description: When a prison is mistaken for a palace, a nation’s tragedy begins.

item.title: Union pushes for health Insurance, safe mining and environmental accountability
item.description: The Zimbabwe Diamond and Allied Workers Union (ZDAMWU) has called for urgent reforms in the mining sector, including compulsory health insurance for workers, stronger safety standards and stricter environmental rehabilitation measures.

item.title: High rents price small traders out of partitioned shops
item.description: Informal traders in Bulawayo say soaring rents for newly partitioned shops are pushing them out of formal trading spaces and back onto the streets, undermining efforts to decongest the city.

item.title: Where is the sugar tax going? MPs press govt over cancer funding
item.description: The government has been challenged to explain how millions of dollars collected through a tax on sugar-sweetened beverages are being used, amid concerns that cancer treatment services remain in a critical state.
